tool.name: rheoTool on OpenFOAM (rheoFoam)
tool.source: rheoTool's user guide (mat-20261121-rheotool-6.0-user-guide), its of90 tutorials and OpenFOAM's own planarPoiseuille tutorial, read on the day their material cards name
tool.language: C++ applications of OpenFOAM driven by case dictionaries
tool.version: the image rheotool:of90 in this computer's Colima profile rheotool, the versions inside it to be read off the adapter's trial
tool.license: GPL for OpenFOAM and rheoTool, as their sources state it (mat-20261121-rheotool-of90-channel-oldroyd-b-constitutive, mat-20261121-openfoam-9-planarpoiseuille-watersking); called out of process, never bundled

claims.claim: rheoTool's Oldroyd-B model (TypeName Oldroyd-B, or Oldroyd-BLog for the log-conformation approach) takes the constants etaS, etaP and lambda in constitutiveProperties, with rho, each a dimensioned value in OpenFOAM's SI dimension set (dynamic viscosity, time, density)
rheoFoam is a transient solver whose momentum equation takes fvOptions, and rheoTool supports cyclic patches, so a channel may be driven by a momentum source with periodic ends

evidence.locus: the user guide, section 4.7.1, the listing of rheoFoam's momentum equation, and the changelog on cyclicAMI (mat-20261121-rheotool-6.0-user-guide)

claims.limitations: the guide's channel tutorial is steady and inlet-driven; a start-up driven by a source is not exemplified in rheoTool, only in OpenFOAM's own planarPoiseuille tutorial (mat-20261121-openfoam-9-planarpoiseuille-watersking)

claims.claim: the analytical velocity of the start-up planar Poiseuille flow of an Oldroyd-B fluid is Waters and King's series in the elasticity number lambda eta0/(rho h^2) and the solvent's share beta, h the half-width and time scaled by lambda
claims.limitations: the original, Waters and King (1970), was not read: no open copy was found

claims.claim: the image rheotool:of90 is in the Colima profile rheotool, which `colima list` showed stopped on 2026-11-21

rheoFoam's momentum equation is written per unit density: the pressure it solves for and the stress term are divided by the density, so a momentum source given to it in fvModels (semiImplicitSource, volumeMode specific) is a force per unit mass, the pressure gradient over the density

evidence.locus: the user guide, section 4.7 on divTau, 'divided by the density to be compliant with the usual strategy of OpenFOAM', and section 5.1.1 on the pressure (mat-20261121-rheotool-6.0-user-guide)
OpenFOAM-9's planarPoiseuille tutorial, constant/fvModels, a semiImplicitSource of volumeMode specific on U (mat-20261121-openfoam-9-planarpoiseuille-watersking, the same tutorial folder)

claims.claim: the run adapter, tried under TMPDIR, sent a periodic planar channel case into rheotool:of90 through stdin, ran blockMesh and rheoFoam there and read back OpenFOAM's probe of the centreline velocity; the series followed oldroyd_b_startup_channel_velocity for the trial's settings, its overshoot and its oscillation included (evidence for the adapter only; no value of it enters a card)

evidence.locus: the adapter's trial under TMPDIR, back/log.rheoFoam and back/postProcessing/probes/0/U of its run folder

claims.limitations: one mesh and one time step; the run's own numerical error is not estimated, which a two-resolution run would give (discretization_error_from_two_resolutions)
